title: Agent Contract
description: What every pluggable agent takes in and must produce, enforced by Harbor. Confirmed empirically: result.json has identical top-level keys whether the agent was 'oracle' or 'mini-swe-agent' — what differs is only the values inside agent_result, not the shape.

input.description: A task spec (task.toml + instruction.md, per the task contract) plus a model handle (the -m flag string, e.g. 'openai/gemini-flash', per the model contract). The agent never receives provider-specific detail — only the LiteLLM alias.

output.description: result.json — same top-level shape regardless of which agent ran, confirmed by diffing sorted keys from an oracle trial and a mini-swe-agent trial on the same task.

config.description: Full trial configuration: task, agent, environment, verifier settings.

name.description: e.g. 'oracle', 'mini-swe-agent', 'opencode' — this is the pluggable part.

agent_result.description: Content varies meaningfully by agent (oracle has near-zero token usage, a real model doesn't) but the field names themselves (n_input_tokens, n_output_tokens, cost_usd, model_usage) are present regardless.

rewards.description: e.g. {"reward": 1.0} — the objective pass/fail score, independent of which agent produced it.

exception_info.description: Present and populated on failures (AgentTimeoutError, NonZeroAgentExitCodeError, etc.), null on clean success. Same field exists either way — its presence/absence, not its shape, signals success vs. failure.
